test a robust DBA combination given the trend-dominated regime and unstable rankings.
use data‑driven weighting for unstable rankings
Test a weight‑based strategy that uses plain inverse‑error weighting on the full pool to see if data‑driven weights beat the mean in this trend‑dominated, ranking‑unstable series.
Test a per‑horizon weighted combination using the top‑k mean handle (w4) to capture horizon‑specific strengths in this trend‑dominated, unstable‑ranking series.

The series has unstable rankings (tau -0.099) and a trend-dominated regime, so a robust but slightly more selective combination than a plain mean may help. A median will reduce influence of extreme models while still aggregating many.
The series shows unstable rankings and strong trend; a per‑horizon best‑model weighting could capture horizon‑specific strengths.
test a weighted combination on a smaller robust pool (trend_dominated, unstable ranking) to see if removing weaker models improves performance.
The series has unstable rankings and a strong trend; a per‑horizon best‑model weighting on a modest pool may capture horizon‑specific strengths.
The series is trend‑dominated with unstable rankings; a simple mean over a smaller, more stable subset (pool4) might yield a robust result.
Try a weighted combination on the smaller, more stable pool4 using softmax‑negative‑error weights to see if a more focused, high‑confidence mix improves over the plain mean.

decision.justification: Selected 'mean' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 1.0. Series context: trend strength 0.7197 and seasonal strength 0.2147; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau -0.099); 6 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.842.
